summary: Set 119 Session 2 makes a close's obligations knowable before it runs. `python -m ai_router.close_preflight` reports every close-out obligation in one pass -- met and unmet, blocking and advisory -- at any point in a session, with NO side effects and NO routed call (no lock, no ledger event, no file written). It **reports; it never refuses**: this set's spec forbids a new gate, so blocking-ness is read from `gate_checks.is_blocking_check` rather than re-derived, and every verdict comes from CALLING the predicate `close_session` calls. The expensive case -- `verification_backstop`, 79 of 214 recorded check-failures, each firing a routed call at close time -- is answered for free by `close_backstop.decide_backstop`, EXTRACTED from `run_close_backstop` (which now consumes it) rather than copied, because a preflight carrying its own spelling of that seven-branch sequence would drift from the close it predicts. A close that would buy a round is reported as a COST WARNING, not a refusal: a backstop round returning VERIFIED closes fine. `--replay-history` ships the measurement as an instrument rather than a one-off query: 186 events, 214 recorded check-failures, 64 belonging to checks Set 116 S3 demoted, 150 still blocking, and the preflight covers 150 of 150. Filtering the ledger to before 2026-08-10T20:28Z reproduces the spec's prediction TO THE DIGIT (184 events, 212 failures, 148 still-blocking, 78 backstop, 122 sessions); the delta is exactly Set 117 Session 1's two close-out failures, recorded after the spec was authored. So the spec's prediction was RIGHT and history grew -- and the strong claim that the remainder is all knowable pre-close is confirmed, not asserted. Verification took five rounds and every one of the eight findings was accepted; none was disputed or dismissed. Four round-1 findings were ONE root cause: `close_session` runs the backstop BEFORE the gate chain and the first cut ran it after, so a no-evidence close was reported as a `verification_integrity` refusal (it is not one -- a VERIFIED backstop writes the very artifact that gate wants) and the backstop's mid-close bookkeeping was not tolerated on a rerun. `evaluate` now mirrors the close's order exactly. Round 2 found the two SET-TERMINAL gates outside `GATE_CHECKS` (path-aware critique, contract gate) were missing entirely. Round 3 found that fixing round 2 had introduced a new defect -- `required` was treated as unconditionally blocking while `close_session` soft-warns on the non-TTY path agents actually use -- and that the JSON surface still said `would_close: true` where the human surface said 'NOT yet decided'. Round 4 rejected the `--session-number` fix for deleting a promised input rather than making it coherent. The final shape satisfies both sides: the flag is an ASSERTION that is checked, never a partial override, so a mixed-session report is unrepresentable and a valid invocation is never refused. Round 5, on the operator's recorded authorization at the enforced bound, returned VERIFIED with 8/8 fix verdicts accepted and zero findings.

reason.specifics: Session 3 edits `close_backstop.py` -- the module this session just refactored -- to make a backstop round write a `discoveryBaselineTree` so `--phase remediation-review` stops refusing with EXIT_USAGE after a backstop-only blocking round. That change lands in the EXECUTION half of `run_close_backstop`, which this session deliberately separated from the DECISION half (`decide_backstop`) that `close_preflight` now depends on; an orchestrator who has just read that seam end to end is least likely to break the preflight while editing beside it. Session 3 also deletes seven modules on a proof-of-unreachability obligation, which is exactly the kind of work where knowing what the close path actually calls -- read directly this session, not inferred -- is worth more than provider diversity. Cross-provider independence is preserved where it matters: verification still routes to a different effective provider.

measurement_step_4.measured_today: 186 closeout_failed events; 214 recorded check-failures; 64 belonging to checks Set 116 S3 demoted to advisory; 150 still blocking; 150 covered by the preflight; 123 sessions with >=1 failure plus 1 unnumbered-event close.
measurement_step_4.verdict: The spec's prediction was CORRECT; the corpus grew. Filtering the ledger to before 2026-08-10T20:28Z reproduces the spec digit for digit. The delta is exactly Set 117 Session 1's two close-out failures (verification_backstop at 20:28:56Z, test_run_fresh at 20:29:47Z), recorded after the spec was authored and roughly two hours before this set's Session 1 began. The spec's strong claim -- that the remaining still-blocking failures are ALL knowable before close-out runs -- is confirmed rather than asserted: coverage is 150/150 today, 148/148 at the spec's cut.
measurement_step_4.instrument_defect_found_and_fixed: Reconciling the session count (123 vs 122) found the one real defect in the instrument: a legacy Set 047 event carries "session_number": 0 and was being counted as a session. Session numbers are 1-based everywhere in this repo, so it is now excluded from the session tally -- while its check-failures still count, because a close really did fail and really did name them -- and discarded events are surfaced as `unnumbered_events` rather than vanishing. Pinned by a falsifier.
measurement_step_4.what_the_replay_does_not_claim: It measures COVERAGE, not outcomes, and says so in its own output: the working trees that produced those failures are gone, so it answers 'would the preflight have named this obligation first?', which for a deterministic read-only predicate is the same question.

notes.verification_loop: 5 rounds: discovery (2 fan-out lenses, 4 blocking), supplementary (1 blocking), remediation-review x2 (2 then 1 blocking), and one operator-authorized remediation-review returning VERIFIED with 8/8 fix verdicts accepted and 0 findings. All 8 findings were ACCEPTED; none was disputed, dismissed, or waived, so there is no adjudicated-minor residual. Cost recorded as $0.00 on every round: this is a Copilot CLI seat, where billed usage is unavailable by design.
operator_decisions_this_session: Extraction over duplication (authority=ai, rubric_line=goal-over-letter): the spec's Touches list for this session does not name close_backstop.py, but its step 2 requires the preflight to evaluate the close's predicates 'by calling them rather than re-implementing them'. `decide_backstop` was extracted rather than copied; `run_close_backstop`'s behaviour is byte-identical and its 51 tests pass untouched.

One authorized verification round past the enforced bound (authority=human, rubric_line=accountability-sign-off, verification_effect=strengthens): at the bound, one Major from round 4 was fixed but unreviewed, its executable acceptance criterion passed verbatim, and the acceptance harness REFUSED to auto-close it on a baseline mismatch (its only pre-fix tree belonged to round 2). The operator authorized exactly one round to review the fix delta; it returned VERIFIED.
notes.test_run_of_record: pytest: 3975 passed, 9 skipped, 0 failed in 617.04s (10:17), run on the frozen tree after the last code change and recorded in test-runs.jsonl (digest e565fea2f7cf). No failures, environmental or otherwise.
notes.session_1_residual_closed: The whitespace-only `evidencePaths` schema/validator parity gap that Session 1 recorded as owed to Session 2 is fixed: `docs/path-aware-critique.schema.json` gives the array item the non-whitespace `pattern` its sibling `description` property already carried. Fail-closed is not the same as in-parity (L-066-1) -- nothing invalid was ever accepted at runtime, but a schema-only consumer would have accepted an artifact the runtime rejects. Both directions are now pinned by falsifier pairs in `test_path_aware_critique_schema.py`.
owed_residuals: The doc-only cap's blast radius is still unmeasured. Session 1 named it; this session did not fold it in because the replay reads `session-events.jsonl` (close-out failures) while that question needs `sN-issues*.json` (findings) -- a different corpus and a different instrument. Still owed.

`EvidenceTooLargeError` is the one pre-metered backstop refusal the preflight does not predict. It is raised by the evidence assembly AFTER `decide_backstop` returns -- the single expensive read in the sequence, deliberately not performed, because assembling evidence on every run would make a run-it-on-a-whim tool no longer cheap. Session 3 touches `close_backstop.py` and could fold it in, but should weigh that cost.

The preflight is discoverable only by a pointer. The constitution sits at 3,984 of its 4,000-token ceiling and ceilings ratchet down only, so the Step 8 pointer row was reworded to name the preflight BEFORE close (evicting nothing) and the narrative lives in `close-out.md` Section 1 and the workflow doc. Anything more is an eviction decision and belongs to the later preload set.
